title: Bug location identified
text: ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__set__ at lines 256-257 in django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py eagerly copies pk value at assignment time instead of lazily resolving it

title: Root cause explained
text: When order.product = Product() is executed, line 257 copies Product().sku (empty string) directly to order.__dict__['product_id']. Later order.product.sku = 'foo' changes the instance's pk but order.product_id is never updated

title: Related code location
text: ForeignKeyDeferredAttribute.__set__ at lines 75-79 handles direct FK value assignment but doesn't help when the value is eagerly set by ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__set__

text: Always run flake8 before submitting patch

title: ForeignKey descriptor data-loss bug fix applied
text: Removed stale value copy logic from ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__set__ in django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py. The fix removes the code that copies field values from the cached object when setting an FK - this was causing order.product_id to become stale when product.pk was modified after assignment.

title: Basic fix verification passed
text: Test output confirmed fix works: after product.save() and order.save(), order.product_id correctly equals 'SKU456' (the new pk) and persists after refresh_from_db().
